    46	Since $(I-H_W)^2\geq0$,
    47	\[
    48	  H_W^2\geq2H_W-I,
    49	  \qquad
    50	  \langle\vartheta,H_W^2\vartheta\rangle\geq1-\delta.
    51	\]
    52	Also $\lVert(I-H_W)\vartheta\rVert^2\leq\delta$, whence
    53	\[
    54	  \lVert H_X\vartheta-H_Z\vartheta\rVert^2\leq4\delta.
    55	\]
    56	Together with $H_XH_Z$ equal to the EPR projection, these estimates give the
    57	required overlap bound, with constants absorbed into the stated
    58	$O(\sqrt\delta)$ error.
    59	
    60	For the final transfer, let $\phi\colon\mathcal H\to\mathcal K$ be an isometry
    61	and set $Q=\phi\phi^\dagger$.  If $N_h$ is the unitary-conjugated extension of
    62	a measurement operator $M_h$, then the exact identity is
    63	\[
    64	  \phi M_h\phi^\dagger=N_hQ=QN_h,
    65	\]
    66	not merely $N_h$.  Thus comparison of $N_h$ with an ideal projector must be
    67	combined with control of $(I-Q)\Delta$ on the ideal comparison state
    68	$\Delta$.
    69	
    70	\section{Numerical defects in the source proof}
    71	
    72	Lines~1715--1742 of
    73	\path{references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex}
    74	construct $H_X,H_Z$ and identify $H_XH_Z$ with the EPR projection.  The norm
    75	estimate at lines~1743--1750 gives
    76	$\lVert(I-H_W)\vartheta\rVert\leq\sqrt\delta$.  At lines~1753--1757 the
    77	source substitutes $\delta$ inside the reverse triangle inequality
    78	\cite[lines~1715--1783]{Ji2020MIPStar}.  That replacement is not valid for
    79	small $\delta$.  The desired lower bound on
    80	$\langle H_W^2\rangle$ follows directly from $H_W^2\geq2H_W-I$, as above.
    81	
    82	The triangle inequality yields
    83	\[
    84	  \lVert H_X\vartheta-H_Z\vartheta\rVert\leq2\sqrt\delta,
    85	\]
    86	so its square is at most $4\delta$.  Line~1761 instead bounds that square by
    87	$2\sqrt\delta$ without a stated restriction.  This inequality follows when
    88	$\delta\leq1/4$; for larger error the theorem is made trivial by enlarging the
    89	universal constant.  The same small-error split ensures that the projected
    90	vector defined at lines~1769--1773 is nonzero before it is normalized.  These
    91	are local numerical repairs and do not weaken the extraction conclusion.
    92	
    93	\section{The range-projection obligation}
    94	
    95	Lines~1827--1858 prove state-dependent closeness for the concrete operators
    96	obtained by conjugating the original measurement with the swap unitaries.
    97	Lines~1864--1875 then define isometries by adjoining EPR pairs and applying
    98	those unitaries, and immediately state the corresponding closeness for
    99	$\phi M_h\phi^\dagger$.  The omitted range projection makes this implication
   100	non-definitional \cite[lines~1827--1875]{Ji2020MIPStar}.
   101	
   102	Let $\Psi$ be the original state and suppose $\phi\Psi$ is close to the ideal
   103	state $\Delta$.  Since $Q\phi\Psi=\phi\Psi$ and $Q$ is a contraction, the
   104	triangle inequality bounds $(I-Q)\Delta$ by the state-extraction error.  Using
   105	$\phi M_h\phi^\dagger=N_hQ$, split
   106	\[
   107	  (N_hQ-T_h)\Delta
   108	  =(N_h-T_h)\Delta-N_h(I-Q)\Delta,
   109	\]
   110	where $T_h$ is the ideal Pauli projector.  Summing squared norms over $h$
   111	uses projectivity and orthogonality to keep the second term under control.
   112	The same argument is required for each player and each Pauli basis.
   113	
   114	The finite-dimensional estimate is proved in
   115	\path{MIPStarRE/QPBT/Test/Soundness/RangeProjection.lean}. For a complete POVM
   116	$\{N_h\}$, an orthogonal projection $Q$, and $Q\vartheta=\vartheta$, it gives
   117	\[
   118	  \sum_h\|(N_hQ-T_h)\Delta\|^2
   119	  \le 2\sum_h\|(N_h-T_h)\Delta\|^2+2\|\Delta-\vartheta\|^2.
   120	\]
   121	The proof uses $\sum_h N_h^\dagger N_h\le I$, so it also applies when the
   122	measurement is not projective. The same module proves the isometry form under
   123	the exact identity $N_h\phi=\phi M_h$ and its two bipartite placements. The
   124	unit-ancilla embedding and its composition with a unitary, including the
   125	identity $U(M\ot I\ot I)U^\dagger\phi=\phi M$, are proved in
   126	\path{MIPStarRE/QPBT/Test/Soundness/Ancilla.lean} for $\phi=UJ$,
   127	$J\psi=\psi\ot\eta$, $\|\eta\|=1$, and $U^\dagger U=I$.
   128	
   129	The supplied-data transfer is proved in
   130	\path{MIPStarRE/QPBT/Test/Soundness/StateTransfer.lean} and
   131	\path{MIPStarRE/QPBT/Test/Soundness/OperatorTransfer.lean}. Given an actual
   132	\path{ExtractionWitness}, the local maps adjoin a normalized EPR state and
   133	apply its swap unitaries. Register reassociation identifies their tensor
   134	action with the witness's transformed state, so its squared distance from
   135	the ideal state is at most $\delta$. The existing swapped total-Pauli POVMs
   136	intertwine with these maps; the two bipartite range-projection estimates
   137	bound each full squared operator-family sum by $4\delta$. Thus the same
   138	\path{PauliSoundnessWitness} satisfies all three soundness estimates at
   139	$\max\{\sqrt\delta,4\delta\}$. This is an auxiliary result with supplied
   140	extraction data, not a new bridge field or a proof of soundness for arbitrary
   141	strategies.
   142	
   143	\section{Blueprint and formalization status}
   144	
   145	The proof of Lemma~\path{lem:qld-unitary} and the soundness proof in
   146	\path{blueprint/src/chapter/ch16_qpbt_extraction.tex} use the corrected
   147	positive-contraction estimate, make the small-error case distinction explicit,
   148	and isolate the range-projection calculation.  The chapter therefore preserves
   149	the source's state and observable conclusions while exposing the omitted
   150	argument.
   151	
   152	The structure \path{ExtractionWitness} in
   153	\path{MIPStarRE/QPBT/Extraction/Unitary.lean} contains only the two-sided
   154	unitarity equations for the concrete swap maps, a normalized auxiliary state,
   155	the transformed-state estimate, and the two-player Pauli-projector comparison.
   156	The theorem \path{exists_extractionWitness_ofGlobalPairWitness} concludes the
   157	existence of this data at the explicit extraction scale, but it takes the
   158	\path{GlobalPairWitness} of Lemma~\path{lem:qld-4-7} as an explicit hypothesis.
   159	It therefore remains a conditional helper rather than a formalization of the
   160	source lemma.  The blueprint records it on the separate formalization-support
   161	node \path{lem:qld-unitary-given-global-pair}, whose statement displays the
   162	global polynomial-pair measurement as supplied data.  The helper is proved at
   163	this conditional statement and has only the standard axioms \path{propext},
   164	\path{Classical.choice}, and \path{Quot.sound}.  Apart from the supplied witness,
   165	its conclusion matches the Stage~4.2 extraction lemma, including the corrected
   166	numerical estimates.
   167	
   168	The preceding global-measurement construction is now complete.
   169	The theorem \path{exists_globalPairWitness} proves the full-domain construction
   170	of Lemma~\path{lem:qld-4-7} for every strategy error, including zero.  The
   171	source-facing theorem \path{exists_pulled_apart_consistency} chooses one such
   172	witness, applies the two point-consistency estimates and the observable
   173	self-consistency estimate to it, and replaces their three universal constants
   174	by their maximum.  Thus Lemma~\path{lem:qld-construct-the-paulis} is proved for
   175	the stated domain $0\leq\epsilon\leq1$, including the zero-error boundary.
   176	
   177	The source-facing theorem \path{exists_extractionWitness} now composes
   178	\path{exists_globalPairWitness} with
   179	\path{exists_extractionWitness_ofGlobalPairWitness}: the universal error
   180	constants for the global measurement and extraction are chosen before the
   181	parameters and strategy. For every admissible parameter tuple and projective
   182	strategy with $0\leq\epsilon\leq1$, it constructs the global pair of
   183	projective measurements internally and obtains a normalized auxiliary state
   184	and two concrete swap unitaries satisfying the state and both players'
   185	Pauli-family distances at the nested construction/extraction scale. This is
   186	the existence claim of Lemma~\path{lem:qld-unitary}; its proof does not
   187	require a supplied global measurement. The general range-projection and
   188	unit-ancilla lemmas apply to the concrete swap operators and Pauli measurements
   189	through the proved supplied-data transfer above. This yields local isometry
   190	comparisons for the extracted projective setting, but does not extend the
   191	construction to arbitrary strategies.
   192	
   193	The stronger theorem \path{exists_extractionWitness_fourth_root_rate}
   194	normalizes the numerical rate of this concrete conclusion to the same
   195	global-measurement parameter. Starting with the global error
   196	$\delta_G^{a_0,b_0}$, the scalar absorption theorem bounds the nested
   197	extraction error by another family member $\delta_G^{a_1,b_1}$. Choose
   198	$a\geq\max\{a_0,a_1+1\}$ and $b=\min\{b_0,b_1\}$. Monotonicity permits the
   199	\emph{same} global measurements to carry the larger consistency certificate
   200	$x=\delta_G^{a,b}$. If $x\leq1$, their established extraction error is at
   201	most $x\leq x^{1/4}$; if $x>1$, the universal four-error construction gives
   202	both estimates. Enlarging the extraction constant to at least four yields
   203	$C(x^{1/4}+md/q)$ in both cases. This normalization concerns the concrete
   204	swap maps only: it neither identifies the seed-indexed low-degree game with
   205	the direct carrier nor establishes soundness for arbitrary strategies. The
   206	separate supplied-data isometry transfer above applies to its witness.
   207	
   208	Issue~\#19 owns this concrete Stage~4.2 interface and discrepancy record.
   209	\ghissue{123} records the source-facing composition work: both the pulled-apart
   210	consistency and the source-unitary existence compositions are proved. Other
   211	issue~\#123 targets remain unfinished; the earlier attempt history is unchanged.
   212	The direct-carrier proof of the global constructor does not discharge the
   213	seed-indexed correspondence and direct-law restrictions documented in
   214	\path{docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_ld-dimension-divisibility.tex}.
   215	\ghissue{47} tracks the separate range-projection transfer needed
   216	by \path{pauli_soundness}; that theorem must be derived from the concrete data
   217	rather than stored in the witness.
   218	\ghissue{529} records the independent general range-projection and ancilla
   219	results. \ghissue{586} applies them to the extracted swap maps and both Pauli
   220	operator families; neither result establishes unrestricted soundness.
   221	Composing the global-pair and extraction construction with this isometry
   222	transfer gives, for every admissible parameter tuple, $0\leq\epsilon\leq1$,
   223	and projective setting, local isometries and a unit auxiliary state whose
   224	state norm and both complete Pauli-family distances have a common
   225	$a(md)^a(\epsilon^b+q^{-b}+2^{-bmd})$ bound. The universal constants are
   226	chosen before the setting; neither global-pair nor extraction data are
   227	assumptions of the resulting theorem. This is the separately labelled
   228	projective-setting support result, not Theorem~\path{thm:pauli}: an arbitrary
   229	successful strategy can now be placed in the required projective setting by
   230	the questionwise Naimark dilation of issue~\#603. That construction preserves
   231	the value and the complete Pauli-answer measurements under ground-slice
   232	compression, and a witness on the dilation pulls back to an original-space
   233	witness with exactly the same extracted state and state distance. Compression
   234	does not identify the projective dilated effects with the conjugates of the
   235	original POVM effects. Transferring both complete operator-family errors,
   236	including any ground-slice leakage, and treating the full source error domain
   237	remain open. The seed-indexed game correspondence remains a separate obligation
   238	recorded in \path{docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_ld-dimension-divisibility.tex}.
   239	\ghissue{602} tracks this restricted composition.
   240	\ghissue{603} tracks the concrete dilation and original-space state pullback.
   241	
   242	\section{Conclusion}
   243	
   244	The printed triangle calculation has repairable numerical errors, and the
   245	last passage from unitaries to isometries omits a genuine range-projection
   246	argument.  Neither defect is a counterexample to Pauli soundness.  The former
   247	is corrected by positive-contraction inequalities and a small-error split;
   248	the latter has a proved general estimate and an application to the concrete
   249	extraction data. The global polynomial-pair witness
   250	and the three pulled-apart consistency estimates are now composed in a proved
   251	source-facing theorem, including at zero error. The conditional extraction
   252	theorem remains useful for a supplied global measurement, and its composition
   253	with the proved global constructor establishes the source-facing existence
   254	claim of Lemma~\path{lem:qld-unitary} for projective strategies. Its concrete
   255	isometry transfer, including the state and both operator estimates, is proved
   256	for supplied extraction data. Composing that transfer with the internally
   257	constructed data proves the restricted projective-setting isometry bounds.
   258	The unrestricted source theorem still requires the complete operator-family
   259	transfer through the dilation, the full error domain, and the source-game
   260	correspondence step; \path{pauli_soundness} remains open.
